      HOW TO WRITE TO OUTLET
      ----------------------
Letters are accepted in any form
for publication in OUTLETTERS:
BASIC PRINT or DATA; handwritten
or typed copy; all wordprocessor
files (please state which!) or a
simple JOTTER program is in our
Issue 2(Disk #4).The easiest for
us to edit are Tasword 2 files
with the right margin set at 32.

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From Malcolm Goodman,  LEEDS

I noticed that ROMANTIC ROBOT
were advertising their MULTIFACE
with +D compatibility so I wrote
to enquire about the cost of
modifying my non +D variety.They
quoted `10.95, all-inclusive. I
sent this off with the unit and
within 3/4 days had a BRAND NEW
version back. Thank you R.R.!!



Thanks, Malcolm. I've still had
no time to study that listing
(for a 48K to 128K "switch") you
sent me but will eventually.

                        - Brian

From J.W. Tollett, HANTS

I want to save TASWORD PLUS TWO
to PLUS D disc;to save textfiles
to disc and print text files.
There is, I'm told, a program
that does all that called TASCON
+2 marketed by FORMAT magazine
run by Bob Brenchley but as I
have received no replies to my
three letters and a cheque I
assume that FORMAT is dead.

I'm afraid I also have another
problem and that is obtaining a
lead to connect my STAR LC10
Centronics printer to my PLUS D
interface. The MGT manual states
this should have a "standard
BBC-type connector" (26-way) for
the PLUS D end.

Radio Spares market an item
under part number 489-992 called
"BBC Micro-to-printer-interface"
Maybe there is someone in your
grup that can advise on whether
this is the correct item to use.
A letter to MGT requesting
assistance did not get a reply.

I cannot thank you enough for
your offer of help and the
knowledge that there is someone
out there willing to help.

        Yours sincerely,

          J.W. Tollett

To Mr. J.W. TOLLETT from Brian



You should,by now, have received
my letter confirming I'm almost
certain the connector IS correct
as I've recently had to buy one
for my SAM COUPE.Can anyone else
doubly-confirm there is only ONE
BBC-standard printer connector?


FORMAT magazine DO offer TASCON
+2 but only to members of INDUG
(who produce FORMAT) so you will
have to join to get the program.


                     - Brian

From Jaap Juursema, NETHERLANDS

Congratulations on passing the
1000-circulation Mark. I wonder,
if you could use some assistance
to reach the 2000-mark by Xmas?
My suggestions...
1.HAPPY READERS, COME TO ACTION!

In my opinion, it is time that
we - me and all the other happy
readers/users lend you a helping
hand. A strong and healthy
Chezron organisation is in the
best interest of our whole
community.Please accept a cheque
as start of the Spectrum-Chezron
Support Group. May many others
follow. Please start a new
monthly Outlet-item named, for
instance, CAMPAIGN-NEWS to keep
us up to date.

2. WHY NOT GO E.E.C. (AND BEGIN
WITH A SMALL COUNTRY SUCH AS THE
NETHERLANDS)?

To make my position clear, I am
just an ordinary member of the
Dutch Hobby Computerclub(H.C.C.)
with no mandate whatsoever. All
the same, I am willing to help
and you at Chezron may think it
could work. please, see my later
suggestions.

As for an approach to the Dutch
Spectrum users, I see three opp-
ortunities that might be useful:

1) The Dutch Disciple News Brief
(D.N.B., circulation 300 copies,
on disc or tape-cassette + 25
pages on paper).

They stopped circulation in the
beginning of this year (just for
family-reasons) so the last
machine-readable magazine for
the Dutch Spectrum community
went out of business.

The editor-in-chief is an
acquaintance of mine. Perhaps
the D.N.B.-mailing list could
still be obtained from him.

2) Sinclair Impuls, the Dutch
Sinclair user group(includes the
Discovery Users Club,circ.500?).
Their periodical's still a paper
only magazine. All their copy is
first assembled/processed as TW-
files,including BASIC- and Gens-
listings. Later on, the copy is
put to paper (approx. 50 pages,
4 times a year.

If you think it useful to get
into contact with the board of
Impuls ( 8 to 10 persons), I
have their addresses available.


3) The (Dutch) Hobby-Computer
Club (H.C.C. , Membership ca.
20.0000 ).Largely P.C.- oriented
gives three to four times a year
an article, specially directed
to the Spectrum community.


An article about Outlet has a
good chance of being placed in
my opinion but we mustn't forget
that the language barrier in the
Netherlands is often higher than
generally thought.

Remarks, in recent issues, that
routines in MEGADEM (OUTLET 33)
may be copyright are correct.
Before publication in the Disci-
ple Nieuwsbrief, I contacted the
editor and obtained permission
to use the named software for a
publication in the Disciple
Nieuwsbrief.After publication,we
sent him a copy of the publicat-
ion accompanied with a thank-you
letter.

The software package"ZX Spectrum
Graphics" of Piers Letcher was
advertised in Your Computer in
1985, if I remember well.In 1986
it was pubished in book form as
part of Kluwer's "Programmeer-
serie, original title:"Step-by-
step Programming ZX Spectrum(+)
Book Three".

So, the D.N.B-publication did
nothing illegal. Further on, as
far as I can see, legal rights
must serve a reasonable purpose.
It remains to be seen,whether
copyright serve a reasonable
purpose when a software-package
is no longer available via the
commercial circuit and neither
constitutes a secret of trade.

        Sincerely yours,

          Jaap Juursema


To Jaap Juursema from Brian

Both Ron and I were overwhelmed
by your generosity and your good
wishes but we cannot accept such
donations and are returning the
payment. We foresee all sorts of
complication in administrating
such a fund and it would only be
likely to raise an amount that,
while welcome, would not make a
substantial difference to our
enterprise.

Our main concern at present is
time and labour and any readers
wishing to support OUTLET would
help us more by contributing any
programs or articles they are
able. OUTLETTERS should be sent
in as text files WHERE POSSIBLE

as much time is wasted retyping
letters the reader has already
typed once! Longer articles MUST
be as some sort of textfile.

Contributed programs should be
tested carefully before sending
and code details and filenames
etc. in the accompanying letter
are helpful.

Readers could also take any
opportunities to give us a plug
say,in a computer club or letter
to a magazine.

Jaap, your other ideas are good
and we'd be delighted if you are
able to get the address list you
mentioned and INPULS address.
                        - Brian

From Ron Smith, LONDON N.9

On the next page is a copy of a
letter to the manufacturers of
the MicroReader which decodes
Morse and RTTY into plain
English via a suitable shortwave
receiver. The MicroReader works
perfectly. It has an RS232 port
for direct connection to a
computer wih an RS232 interface
which the +3 has via the IDC
socket Midi/serial. The Micro-
Reader defaults to 4800 baud but
can be altered to 600, 1200,
2400 or 4800.The program listing
should print on-screen the
received data via the serial
port of the MicroReader to the
+3 but the screen remains blank.
Can you assist me?

10 REM reads data from RS232
20 FORMAT LINE 4800
30 FORMAT LPRINT "R"
40 OPEN #4,"P"
50 PRINT INKEY$ #4;
60 GOTO 50

LETTER TO MANUFACTURERS:-
"This letter relates to my phone
call re serial interfacing with
the Spectrum +3. I have included
the wiring instructions to IDC
plug for your information...

RS232 socket:-
pin 1.Ground
pin 2.TXD
pin 3.RXD
pin 4.DTR (data terminal ready)
pin 5.CTS (clear to send)
pin 6.+12v

I have joined the wires of pins
4 and 5 together as advised in
the Spectrum manual as there is
no handshaking required;disabled
the wire from pin 3 and 6 and
made safe. I soldered pins 1 and
3 to a 3.5 jack plug pin 1 to
outer terminal pin 3 to centre
terminal."


The BASIC and wiring agree with
the info in the +3 manual but I
wonder if the "P" at line 40
should be changed to "R"? It's
worth a try in case there's a
misprint in the manual. I can't
help if it's a wiring fault so
let's hope you get help from the
manufacturers or perhaps another
OUTLET reader can advise?
                       - Brian

Dear R & B,

As an early SAM owner(one of the
first 4000), I became an OUTLET
subscriber because I found your
SAM COUPE cover so much more
comprehensive than any other
source. Recent experience has
confirmed the wisdom of my deci-
sion. Since MGT have apparently
ceased to operate their HOTLINE
there has been little or no
reliable information as to the
prospects for SAM. Thank you,
therefore, for the STOP PRESS on
the situation which accompanied
OUTLET 35.

The news that, despite repeated
promises and assurances,issue of
version 2 ROMs and DOSs will not
be completed [as planned] will
come as a severe disappointment
to owners, particularly those
whose names commence with a
letter late in the alphabet even
though,like myself,they may have
bought their machines months
earlier and long before lucky
owners who now possess the
replacements.This is, of course,
if in fact, any start had been
made on distribution on alpha-
betic- or any other basis- which
now seems dubious.

I have seen the replacements re-
ferred to as "freebies". As they
were replacements for unsatis-

factory items which were of
"non-merchantable quality" and
"unfit for the purpose" to quote
the Sales of Goods and Services
Act, they are NOT "freebies" but
legally required in order to
satisfactorily complete the con-
tract of sale. It is to be hoped
that a new company taking over
SAM will recognize this and hon-
our their responsibility towards
the 4000-odd SAM owners who are
in possession of machines which
may not be able to use the
software now beginning to appear
and whose disc drives require
tedious and repetitive key calls
to get into operation.

The "limbo" situation meantime
means SAM owners are completely

dependent upon each other for
the sort of advice and help
normally available from the
supplier. Can I, therefore, use
your columns to seek advice upon
a situation with my SAM used
with a Phillips CM8833 monitor?


When the screen colour is white
or a light colour, a series of
narrow, vertical dark columns
can be seen. Any black or dark
letters have a faint but dist-
inct complete shadow displaced
about an inch to the right of
the original. It is very similar
to the "double-vision" effect on
normal television reception that
is usually put down to aerial
reflection or "sound-on-vision".

The effect can be reduced but
not eliminated by manipuation of
the monitor controls and is also
present if a Ferguson MC01 TV/
monitor is used.

Other owners I have consulted
have noticed this phenomenon. I
wondered if the radiation from
the computer and/or modulator
referred to by Frank Harrop in
Issue 35 is in any way connect-
ed.

I have certainly experienced
another effect of this radiation
in that reception on any radio
receiver operated on VHF within
about 30ft of the computer is
completely swamped by interfer-
ence while the computer is on.

Any advice on how to improve the
screen presentation by getting
rid of the shadows would be
greatly appreciated.

            Regards,

          Les Phillips

To Les Phillips from Brian

You are absolutely right that
the new ROMs should not have
been referred to as "freebies"
as though MGT were doing us all
a favour! Statements apparently
issuing from MGT seem calculated
to incense their customers. In
the latest SHOPPER is the claim:
"there is nothing intrinsically
faulty about the original ROM
chip but that the new versions
do contain improvements". I have
to regard that as an outrageous
lie. Another statement in one of
the weeklies not too long ago
said something like MGT "had
found a bug in the ROM" as if
(a) it had just been discovered
and (b) there was only one!

We have invested much effort and
capital in the SAM COUPE. It is
in our interests to promote the
machine but we must report the
facts - not fiction. In the long
run, nobody is served well by
being misled.

Now, as for the monitor problem
I wonder if you get the same
using the tv modulator output to
an ordinary television? I had a
similar effect (using tv) on my
first SAM but it is not present
on the replacement. It does seem
you'll have to wait for the MGT
situation to resolve itself and
return the machine for repair. I
would try moving the SAM about -
up, down, tilting and towards
and away from the monitor to see

if this has any influence on the
ghosting. It's unlikely but you
might as well experiment and
eliminate. Do the same with the
PSU - even though you are not
using the modulator it is giving
out a signal.

Have any other readers had this
problem or can anyone offer any
other suggestions?
                      - Brian

From David Stewart, AYRSHIRE

Here are a few observations on
my Spectrum emulator (EMUTILITY)
published last month (SAM OUTLET
34 only). Most importantly, the
extra code and the paging bug
mean that it won't run under the
old ROM(well properly!).

Your "RAMSAVE" is a great idea -
especially for tape users - but
I did have a couple of reserv-
ations... The first was purely a
matter of taste (i.e. ignore!) -
I don't like the program
automatically running! The main
problem is with programs saved
with the wrong interrupt setting
which"crash" on loading. RAMSAVE
will still hold a copy but under

some circumstances a"crash" will
take part of the ROM with it.

Regarding the second version of
the program,I think the"multiple
NMI bypass" fails occasionally
due to incompatible interrupt
status - I was surprised to find
Z80 NMI's could be interrupted!
Multiple NMI's aren't really a
problem with disk anyway and the
new style buttons ought to get
rid of the problem.

All in all though, I think any
problems are trivial and you did
a great job in converting it!
              - David Stewart

Hope everyone has a new ROM soon
as EMUTILITY is a super program!
                         - Brian

From K.A. Schimmel, NOTTINGHAM


Dear Brian,

When you published SUPERMAT (in
OUTLET 26) I FORMATTed my spare
discs and instead of using tape
to back up MASTERFILES I began
using a disk and found after a
few updates,ERASEs and SAVES,one
disk gave the dreaded "missing
address mark".

After it happened for the third
time and my hair was beginning
to get thinner, I looked a bit
deeper into it and found the
disks which failed were SUPERMAT
disks and my original MF disk
was NORMALLY formatted.

disks I came to the conclusion:
SUPERMAT disks are O.K. if used
for programs which require only
loading (I have about 20 of them
and none has caused any trouble)
but, are not suitable for disks
which require frequent updating
(ERASEing and SAVEing).

I also made some other trials:

Switching OFF with disk in drive

     173K - O.K every time
     192K - Failed 1 in 3

Switching ON with disk in drive:

     173K - failed 2 out of 3
     192K   failed EVERY time


Using reset button with disk in
drive:

     173K   failed 1 out of 5

     192K   almost every time.

Well, Brian, I hope you can make
some sense of my pigeon Engish
which I learnt in the cotton
fields of ARKANSAS.

          K.A. Schimmel

I've not had such problems. What
about other readers?Incidentally

35) to format OUTLET discs. I've

From Malcolm Phillips

Dear Ron+Brian,

Just a short note that may help
others who have added a second
drive to their SAM Coupe and
keep getting the error report
"No such drive" or words to that
effect. A simple poke does the
job. Merely poke dvar2,208 and
then resave the dos code. Dvar2
refers to drive 2 and the 208 is
the number of tracks (80) plus
the number of sectors (128) ie
208.
                Malcolm Phillips

Thanks Malcolm and I've passed a
note to Ron to send you a new
yellow wallet.
                     - Brian

From Mike Haine, LEAMINGTON SPA


Dear Ron,

I obtained copies of the two
LERM programs "SAMTAPE" and
"TOOLKIT V2". I find the former
to provide a very easy means of
converting Spectrum programs to
use on SAM. I already had David
Stewart's routines but found
them a bit messy. The Tool kit
hasn't been converted for SAM
(as yet) but with the help of
the second prog on the SAMTAPE
("SAMSPEC") which can be used to
convert BASIC programs and asso-
ciated code routines, the parts
of the toolkit can be loaded so
as to run.

They include a very adequate
assembler and monitor, a
disassembler with "single-step"
mode as well as "CTOS" which is
a very useful facility making it
easy to generate a source code
from a disassembled listing.

I've used SAMSPEC to put Tasword
2 on SAM with my modified BASIC.
However,I had previously ordered
the SAM version of Tasword 2
from Tasman and now use it. I am
altering the BASIC to include
the facilities I had in my own
version.

I have also added two-column
printing. This turned out to be
very simple and only required an
extra 3 lines of BASIC. This was

because the print routines are
all controlled from BASIC with a
call which pokes in the line
address and then prints one 64
charline. Thus, FOR N=10 TO 30
:POKE...:CALL:NEXT N will print
lines 10 to 30.The mods to print
in 2 columns can now specify the
start and end lines - also the
number of copies required.
           Best Wishes,
               - Mike Haine

Many thanks Mike. We have had a
tremendous response to your 3-
column print routine (called
TABLOID in OUTLET) with several
people asking for a Tasword Two
version. Is that possible? I'm
not sure how since Tasword is 64
columns by default. Any ideas?
                        - Brian

From Clifford Cooper, BRIGHTON,



Dear Ron & Brian,

I'd Just like to say how much I
enjoy OUTLET. I look forward to
it every month.


My main reason for writing (pix-
eling) is to do with my Spectrum
+2 (grey model) and my new +D.
When I turn the computer on with
the +D in, the menu half drawn
just freezes. The menu does work
occasionally. I have to keep
pressing Reset until it does.The
menu works more often when the
computer has warmed up a bit.

When the menu does work and I
try and go into the 128K editor
it either crashes, freezes or
(once in a blue moon) it works
for a little while then crashes
but if I go into 48K from the
menu, disc operation is alright.

I telephoned Bob (FORMAT). He
said it's probably a faulty Plus
D. So I sent it back to MGT,
thinking it would take 2-3
weeks. It took less than 2 days!
(I sent it Wednesday afternoon
and received it Friday morning -
unbelievable!!)

There was a note with the inter-
face saying replaced FDC chip
tested/working O.K. I tried it.
It was still the same problem as
before.

I telephoned the engineer who
said he remembered the repair
and it worked on a 128K Spectrum
so get my +2 checked.My +2 seems
alright without the +D. But the

### Сообщение от Brian Gaff о загадочной надписи: «I'M A +3!»

На +3 наберите `COPY RANDOMIZE`, но пока не нажимайте ENTER. Положите пальцы на клавиши C, J и L, быстро нажмите ENTER, а затем сразу зажмите C, J и L вместе — и на экране крупными мигающими буквами появится надпись: «HELLO, I'M A +3». Возможно, придется попробовать разок-другой, чтобы поймать момент.

Вот еще один секрет. Зажмите RESET и BREAK одновременно, чтобы появился тестовый экран (test card), а затем нажмите вместе клавиши Q, A, Z, M, L, P для запуска тестовой программы. (Обратите внимание на предупреждение: продолжение теста может испортить дискету в дисководе!).
